requirements.statement: When the work builds on a feature merged in the last day or two (read from the base branch's git history), /plan's investigation lists what that predecessor already provides and flags each planned task that rebuilds or re-tests it; with no such predecessor found, nothing is flagged. Must pass: yes.

Before tasks are written, /plan states the change's size as a count of files touched, and when the description's acceptance criteria ask for much more machinery than that size supports, the readout says 'the description asks for X beyond the change; kept / cut' and records the decision. Must pass: yes.

Step 4's weight decision uses the stated size and the delta, so over-specified criteria do not raise the weight by themselves; a criterion the owner marked must-pass is never cut by this rule. Must pass: not marked.
The vendored .claude/commands/plan.md is byte-identical to packages/core/commands/plan.md.
A new sub-step 2e.1, directly after 2e's grounding, states 'size: <n> files touched' before any task is written.
Sub-step 2e.1 finds a recent predecessor with git log on the base branch over the touched files, lists what it already provides, and flags tasks that rebuild or re-test it.
Sub-step 2e.1 holds the description's own criteria to 2f's suspicion, writing one 'the description asks for <X> beyond the change; kept / cut' line per item, never cutting a must-pass criterion.
Step 4 gains a paragraph: weigh the 2e.1 size and delta, not the description's list.
The Readout section says DECISIONS carries the 'beyond the change' lines.
'Marked must-pass' means the owner's marking (brief or description), never the Must pass column /plan itself fills in later.
On the spec path (Step 2g, a source that already lists criteria), scope is locked: a criterion beyond the change is reported, never cut.
The kept/cut lines go in the TRD's ## Decision section as well as the readout's DECISIONS.
Step 4 weighs the size restated after 2f, since 2f can absorb blockers after the size is stated.
No change to plan-weight.js, fix-plan.js or any library: weight stays a judgment.
No numeric threshold and no day-count constant.
No change to 2f's absorbed-scope or audit-finding rules beyond a cross-reference.
The step-3 grep prints a non-zero count.
